disprovenClaims: CLAIM: the plan's D4-local text — that Ballistics.Step mirrors Projectile.Update exactly (semi-implicit Euler). DISPROVEN by arithmetic: Euler's error is 0.5*g*dt*T, about 0.33 m at 30 Hz over 2 s against a 0.0625 m quantization step, so the plan's own ABulletFollowsTheSameArcAtAnyTimestep could not have passed against the integrator the plan described. The two statements are mutually inconsistent and the integrator was changed instead.

CLAIM: the plan's Task 9 — that ThrowGrenade has zero consumers repo-wide. DISPROVEN by the compiler: two test files referenced it. The substantive claim (no gameplay producer or consumer) held; the grep claim did not.

CLAIM: the plan's Task 1 table — that ProjectileKind should be created under Ironfront.Net.Replication.Projectiles. DISPROVEN by the codebase: it already exists in Ironfront.Net.Protocol, and a second one is the duplicate-enum defect VehicleDespawnReason was already consolidated out of.
CLAIM: V3's recorded decision that S_PROJECTILE_SPAWN needs no projectile id. DISPROVEN by V7-D6 and V7-D8, which both re-parameterize a live projectile and are meaningless without one.

CLAIM (mine, caught by review): that channel-2 ordering makes an id quarantine unnecessary. The ordering argument is true but defends the wrong hazard — the live exposure is server-vs-client lifetime divergence, which ordering cannot address. Corrected to match on (id, kind) and the spec now states necessary-but-not-sufficient.

CLAIM (mine, caught by review): that ShouldReAnnounce distinguished a heal from the ordinary countdown. It compared against the last ANNOUNCED value rather than the client's prediction, so a resting medipack re-announced continuously.
unverifiedClaims: Bandwidth stays inside criterion 9 at 16 players + 32 bots + 12 vehicles. The per-message payload is pinned against the shared rate constant, but framing, the channel envelope and per-recipient broadcast fan-out are not measured, and no load run was performed.
Tick p99 < 33 ms with the projectile stepper active (criterion 9/10). Not measured, and largely moot while AuthoritativeFlight is off.
A headless server survives launch, flight, impact, detonation and deployable expiry with zero NREs (criterion 11). No headless run was performed.

Weapon.Configuration.releaseDelay = 0.6 s matches the throw clip's animation-event time. Not read from the Editor. The consequence is worse than the plan states: offline stays on the animation event and the server on the constant, so a mismatch relocates the divergence to offline-vs-server rather than removing it.

The Unity-side copies of the integrator in Projectile.Update and GrenadeProjectile.Update stay in step with Ballistics.Step. They are kept aligned by hand and already differ in one respect — they read Physics.gravity where the library hard-codes (0,-9.81,0). Recorded in Ballistics' own remarks.
missingProof: Ten tests named in the plan's Task 10 table are not written: all four grenade tests, all three throwable tests, and AProjectileSpawnRoundTripsAtTwentyBytes by that name (the 20-byte size and hex round-trip ARE covered by the existing conformance tests under different names). The grenade and throwable behaviours are Unity MonoBehaviours with no EditMode harness in this phase.
No two-client session was run, so grenade detonation parity across peers is asserted by construction (the blast position is authoritative and arrives in S_EXPLOSION) rather than observed.
The client prefab array on NetClientProjectilePresenter is unauthored, so nothing has rendered a replicated projectile end-to-end.
reachableRegressions: Pre-V7 a server-side ammo bag and medipack resupplied through InvokeRepeating. That is now gated to NetContext.IsOffline and the replacement runs through ServerDeployableAuthority, which is driven and now has both a Deploy caller and a pose driver — but the end-to-end path is unobserved, so a server-side resupply that silently does nothing is the most likely residual regression.

Offline bullet drop changes for every weapon, by design and recorded. Offline hit registration also changes because the swept segment is no longer doubled. Both were accepted under brainstorm D8; neither has an offline regression test that CI can run.

A throw ordered and then holstered inside the release delay used to fire anyway; that is fixed, but the fix relies on Weapon.Holster and Weapon.Drop being the only interruption paths, which was verified by reading rather than by running.
